from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light waves can superimpose and interfere.",
            "Constructive interference happens when peaks align.",
            "Destructive interference occurs when peaks meet troughs."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Wave Superposition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup waves for animation
        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=BLUE)
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=RED)
        sum_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Position in grid (improving utilization as per issues)
        self.place_in_area(wave1, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(wave2, "E4", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Tracker for animation
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_waves(mob):
            # Using the established grid positions, just oscillating slightly around them
            t = tracker.get_value()
            wave1.move_to(self.grid["B5"] + RIGHT * t * 0.5)
            wave2.move_to(self.grid["E5"] - RIGHT * t * 0.5)

        wave1.add_updater(update_waves)
        wave2.add_updater(update_waves)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(wave1), FadeIn(wave2))
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(sum_wave, "C3", "D5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_wave))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(wave2.animate.set_color(GREEN))

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Holography uses a two-beam interference technique.",
            "A laser splits into object and reference beams.",
            "They combine on a sensitive plate.",

            "This is the hologram's coded data."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Holographic Recording Process", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        laser_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg")

        # Position using revised grid coordinates
        self.place_at_grid(laser_icon, 'B2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(object_icon, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(plate_icon, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Interference Pattern
        interference = VGroup(*[
            Line(plate_icon.get_top(), plate_icon.get_bottom()).set_stroke(YELLOW, width=2)
            for _ in range(10)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).move_to(plate_icon.get_center())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(laser_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        beam_obj = Line(laser_icon.get_right(), object_icon.get_left(), color=RED)
        beam_ref = Line(laser_icon.get_right(), plate_icon.get_left(), color=RED)
        self.play(Create(beam_obj), Create(beam_ref))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(object_icon), FadeIn(plate_icon))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", [
            "Holography is essentially frozen diffraction interference.",
            "Reconstruction brings the 3D scene back.",
            "Security holograms demonstrate this complex principle."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        fringe_pattern = VGroup(*[Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT * (i * 0.2)) for i in range(-5, 6)])
        self.place_in_area(fringe_pattern, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(fringe_pattern))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(cube), FadeOut(fringe_pattern))
        self.play(Rotate(cube, angle=PI/2, axis=UP + RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/creditcard.svg"
        if os.path.exists(asset_path):
            security_icon = SVGMobject(asset_path)
        else:
            # Fallback if asset not found in runtime
            card = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.5, color=GREY, fill_opacity=1)
            label = Text("SECURITY", font_size=24, color=BLACK)
            security_icon = VGroup(card, label)
            
        hologram = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        security_icon_group = VGroup(security_icon, hologram).arrange(DOWN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(security_icon_group, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(security_icon_group), FadeOut(cube))
        self.play(hologram.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Holography and Diffraction

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Wave Superposition
sections.content: Briefly recall how light waves interfere. Use an animation showing two coherent waves overlapping to create constructive and destructive interference patterns.
sections.example: Visualize two ripples in a pond merging; where peaks meet, the water rises higher (constructive); where a peak meets a trough, the water stays flat (destructive).

sections.title: Diffraction: Bending Around Barriers
sections.content: Define diffraction as the phenomenon where waves spread out after passing through an aperture or around an obstacle. Focus on the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern.
sections.example: Imagine a cat peering through a tiny slit in a door; the light waves 'bend' and spread into the room, revealing that light behaves like a wave, not just a straight-line particle.

sections.title: The Holographic Recording Process
sections.content: Explain the two-beam interference technique. A coherent laser beam is split into a reference beam and an object beam. Their interference pattern is captured on a photographic plate (the hologram).
sections.example: Think of a security scanner: the reference beam acts as the 'standard,' while the object beam 'scans' the 3D surface. The resulting pattern on the plate is the 'coded' data of the object.

sections.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the Wavefront
sections.content: Explain how illuminating the hologram with the original reference beam diffracts the light to reconstruct the original wavefront, creating a 3D virtual image.
sections.example: Like playing a vinyl record where the groove represents the 'interference pattern'; shining the light is the 'needle' that brings the 3D 'music' (image) back to life.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that holography is essentially 'frozen' diffraction interference. Connect this to modern technology.
sections.example: Discuss how credit card security holograms work: they are complex diffraction gratings that reveal different images depending on the viewing angle, making them nearly impossible to forge.
